_comment: A completed policy review, kept as a worked example. Target: plugins/format-guard/, the artifact in this catalog that registers a hook. A verdict on a skill-only artifact teaches nothing — the interesting fields (hooks, telemetry, scope) are only exercised by an artifact that can actually reach beyond its own invocation. Reviewed against prompt.md; shape defined by schema.json.
summary: Registers one PostToolUse hook matching Edit|Write that runs hooks/format.sh with the edited file path. The script walks up from the edited file to find a project root that declares a formatter (.prettierrc, or [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml) and runs that formatter on that one file. With no declared formatter it exits 0 without acting. Also ships a /format command that formats the working-tree diff on demand. No network calls, no reads outside the edited file and the formatter config it finds.
hooks: PostToolUse:hooks/format.sh — gated (matcher Edit|Write, plus a declared-formatter check inside the script) — network:no
_notes: may_download_additional_software is false by a narrow margin: `npx --no-install prettier` was the deciding detail. Without --no-install, npx would fetch prettier from the network on a machine that does not have it, which is both a download and an undisclosed network call. Reviewers should check that flag specifically.

has_broad_scope_hooks is false because the hook has two independent gates: the Edit|Write matcher, and the declared-formatter check. Invariant I14 enforces only the first one mechanically — a matcher is checkable, 'relevant to the stated purpose' is not. That judgment is exactly what this layer exists for.

The script reads a file path out of the hook payload with sed rather than a JSON parser. That is a robustness question, not a policy one: a malformed path yields an empty match and the script exits 0. Raise it in code review, not here.
